drivingQuestion: From where do we know that one lacking atonement disqualifies the service?

segments.he: מְחוּסַּר כִּיפּוּרִים מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכִפֶּר עָלֶיהָ הַכֹּהֵן וְטָהֵרָה״ – ״טָהֵרָה״ מִכְּלָל שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that rites performed by «one who has not yet» brought «an atonement» offering to complete the purification process are disqualified. The Gemara asks: «From where do we» derive this? «Rav Huna says: The verse states» with regard to the offering brought by a woman who has given birth: «“And the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be pure”» (Leviticus 12:8). Since the verse states: “And «she shall be pure,”» one learns «by inference that she is ritually impure» to some extent until she brings her offering, even though she has already immersed. Anyone who has not yet brought an atonement offering is likewise impure to some extent, and rites performed by one who is impure are disqualified (see 17a).
